Named for Callimachus, who built the first catalogue of the Library of Alexandria.

Grab the latest signed build from **Releases**: macOS (`.dmg`, Apple Silicon), Windows (`.msi` or `-setup.exe`), or Linux (`.AppImage`, `.deb` or `.rpm`). The app auto-updates from there on. Prefer to build it yourself? See Develop.

Adding another source is a small, documented contract.

- **Stays current** via a background file watcher, plus a catch-up pass at launch for the sessions your agents wrote while the app was closed; **stays private**: the index never leaves your machine, API keys live in the OS keychain, conversation content goes only to an AI provider you pick, and usage analytics are opt-in and content-free (see Security & privacy).

The `--ignored` tests touch live data on this machine: each source has a `real_ _index` smoke test that indexes your real history read-only (`~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, Cursor, `~/.gemini`, `~/.qwen`, Goose, OpenCode, Continue, Cline/Roo/Kilo), plus the embedding-model download (first run, needs network) and a Keychain round-trip.

**MCP server**: let any agent search its own past work mid-session. It reads the index the desktop app builds and does not index anything by itself, so install the app and let it index once first. The quickest way to register it is `npx` (it downloads the prebuilt binary on first run and verifies its SHA-256); it's also listed on the official MCP registry as `io.github.BetaBots-LLC/callimachus`:

Already running the desktop app? You don't need npm: **Settings → Claude Code → Enable for Claude Code** registers the app itself (launched with `--mcp`) as Claude Code's MCP server, and **Settings → Other agents** does the same for Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI. The app keeps those entries pointed at itself after an update or a move. You can also download the standalone `callimachus-mcp-<target>` binary from Releases, or build from a checkout with `cargo install --locked --path apps/desktop/src-tauri --bin callimachus-mcp`.

Tools (22), read **and** write. Reads (18): `search_threads`, `search_current_project` (auto-scoped to the repo it runs in), `recent_threads`, `get_thread`, `list_tags`, `list_open_todos`, `get_thread_knowledge`, `recall_decisions`, `recall_gotchas`, `find_prior_work` (the "have I done this before?" guard: prior sessions similar to a task), `project_memory` (a project's aggregated decisions / gotchas / open TODOs), `ask_history` (a cited RAG answer over your history), `threads_for_file` (which sessions touched a path), `check_decision` (surface settled decisions before re-litigating a proposal), `linked_commits` (the commits a thread likely produced), `recurring_issues` (errors you keep hitting across sessions), `list_snapshots` (a project's session snapshots), and `load_snapshot` (restore a saved checkpoint). Writes (4, into Callimachus's own memory, never your code): `complete_todo` (close an open TODO), `record_decision` (optionally with a `rationale`), `record_gotcha` (persist a fact into a project's memory), and `snapshot_session` (checkpoint a thread for handoff). The bundled `/recall` skill (resources/recall/SKILL.md) tells agents when to reach for them.

**CLI**: `cal`, pipe-friendly. The desktop app installs it with **Settings → Claude Code → Enable for Claude Code**: on macOS and Linux it is linked at `~/.local/bin/cal` (if `~/.local/bin` isn't on your shell's `PATH`, as on stock macOS, Settings shows the `export PATH=...` line to add), and on Windows it is placed as `cal.exe` next to the app. If another program already owns `~/.local/bin/cal`, or a per-machine Windows install can't write `cal.exe`, Callimachus leaves `cal` out and says so in Settings; the hooks, MCP server and `/recall` skill work without it. You can also download the standalone `cal-<target>` binary from Releases, or build from a checkout with `cargo install --locked --path apps/desktop/src-tauri --bin cal`.

**VS Code / Cursor**: the extension adds a "Callimachus History" sidebar, a status-bar search button, and commands to search / insert / copy threads (it shells out to `cal`). `tls_cert` and `domain_expiry` use `warn_days` / `critical_days` thresholds and surface `days_remaining` plus registrar / cert subject in the result payload. Their floors are 1 hour for `tls_cert` and 12 hours for `domain_expiry`, regardless of plan — these probes track values that change on a scale of days, not minutes, and RDAP rate-limits by source address. `flow` runs a real browser, so it only executes where a browser engine is available (its regions clamp to the flow-capable set) and the number of flow monitors is capped per plan; put credentials in an org secret and reference them as `{{name}}`. **ClickHouse system logs are off.** Stock ClickHouse keeps two dozen `system.*_log` tables that grow without bound and use CPU at idle. A stack started before this setting existed keeps its old tables: run `docker compose up -d` first so ClickHouse restarts with the setting, then list them with `SELECT name, formatReadableSize(total_bytes) FROM system.tables WHERE database = 'system' AND name LIKE '%\_log%'` and remove each with `DROP TABLE system.<name>`.
